description: A business is in a dispute with a contractor over a failed delivery. Conflict: The contract has ambiguous 'Force Majeure' clauses. The business wants a full refund; the contractor offers credit. The user needs to negotiate a settlement to avoid a lawsuit.

user_profile.context: Legal letters have been exchanged, trying to avoid court
user_profile.communication_style: Formal, legalistic, but looking for an 'out'

fact_sheet.fact: The business entity in the dispute is 'Acme Innovations Inc.'
The business owner representing Acme Innovations is its CEO, Mr. Julian Vance.
The contractor in the dispute is 'LogiCore Solutions LLC.'
LogiCore Solutions is represented by its legal counsel, Ms. Evelyn Reed of 'Reed & Barton Legal Group'.
The governing contract is identified by the reference number AC-LC-2023-0815.
The contract was signed by both parties on August 15, 2023.
The contracted deliverable was one custom-built 'LC-Custom-Rack-42U' server rack.
The agreed-upon delivery deadline stipulated in the contract was October 30, 2023.
Section 7.2 of the contract defines a 'Force Majeure' event as 'unforeseeable events beyond reasonable control, including acts of God, governmental actions, and significant supply chain disruptions.'
Section 9.1 specifies a penalty of 1.5% of the total contract value for each week of delay, capped at 15%.
The total value of the contract is $28,500.00 USD.
Acme Innovations made a 50% upfront payment of $14,250.00 on August 18, 2023.
The upfront payment was made via wire transfer with confirmation number WT-983451.
Acme Innovations has formally requested a full cash refund of the $14,250.00 payment.
To date, Acme Innovations has incurred $2,150.00 in legal consultation fees with the firm 'Vance & Associates'.
LogiCore Solutions first notified Acme Innovations of a potential delivery delay via email on October 27, 2023.
LogiCore Solutions formally invoked the 'Force Majeure' clause in a certified letter dated November 5, 2023.
Acme Innovations sent its formal letter of dispute, rejecting the Force Majeure claim, on November 15, 2023.
LogiCore's official response, which contained the offer for store credit, was received on December 1, 2023.
The event cited by LogiCore as a Force Majeure incident was a fire at their primary sub-supplier, 'Precision Metals Fab Inc.'
The fire at Precision Metals Fab Inc. occurred on October 25, 2023.
The facility of Precision Metals Fab Inc. is located at 18 Industrial Way, Grand Rapids, MI.
Acme's counter-argument is that LogiCore had a pre-approved alternative supplier, 'SteelForm Components', who was not affected by the fire.
The primary point of contact for this matter at LogiCore Solutions is Mr. David Chen, Head of Operations.
Mr. David Chen's business email address is d.chen@logicore-sol.com.
The internal dispute reference number used by LogiCore's system is 'LC-DISP-77B-2023'.
The most recent direct communication was a phone call between Julian Vance and David Chen on December 5, 2023, at 2:15 PM EST.
During the call on December 5, 2023, Mr. Chen stated that the offer of store credit was 'final and non-negotiable'.
LogiCore's current and only settlement offer is $14,250.00 in store credit, valid for 24 months.
Acme's initial demand was a full cash refund of $14,250.00 plus a 5% penalty for breach of contract.
Acme's most recent pre-litigation settlement offer, sent December 10, 2023, is for a cash refund of $12,000, with both parties waiving all further claims.
No formal lawsuit has been filed by either party as of today's date.
Section 12.4 of the contract specifies that the jurisdiction for any legal action shall be the State of Delaware.
The deadline set by LogiCore Solutions for Acme Innovations to accept the store credit offer is December 20, 2023.
